hypothesis: Native helper positions and a bounded globe radius can fit separate optical layers to unchanged eyelids.
implementedComponents: two independent eye bones parented to head

fitDiagnosis.classificationLimit: Nearest body contacts are classified using frontal ray visibility only; this does not prove all viewing angles are clear.

visualAssessment: The eyes establish a visible gaze and are separated into optical components, but the collision gate fails for all sizes.
A bright crescent at the lower iris and large stage-light reflections keep the eyes from reading as realistic.
Eye sockets and lid contact need their own surface-fit step; shrinking the globe is not accepted as a finished solution.
decision: Retain all three candidates as rejected fit studies. Continue building from r0005, using r0006 component construction only as research input.
nextAction: Repair the native recessed socket faces from the localized contact sets while constraining visible lid/face vertices. Keep an anatomically consistent globe size, then verify both gaze directions, head motion, and body self-intersection before any adoption.
